_comment: Format registry (D45) — the single source of truth for Article Type. Read by packages/engine/src/formats.ts, scripts/formats.py and the web app. Each format's writing guidance lives in templates/formats/<slug>.md (templates/formats/generic.md until one is written). Precedence for FAQ counts (D49): page role (pillar/hub) > the format's own faq > the funnel rule > defaults. Page role also wins the length band for hubs (routing pages, D47). Passages are coverage requirements, not an outline (D33); {subject} and {title} are filled per row.

formats.label: Pillar Guide
passages: A 50–80 word answer defining {subject} that can be lifted verbatim
A full definition of {subject}, self-sufficient even though a child definition page exists
One section per sub-theme that answers its own question completely, then links down to the child page
How {subject} works, as a numbered sequence
A cluster map linking every child page with its head term as the anchor

formats.label: Definition / Explainer
passages: A 40–60 word definition of {subject} that is extractable with zero surrounding context
How {subject} differs from the nearest neighbouring term
The components or types of {subject}, as a list or table
Common misconceptions about {subject}

formats.label: Deep-dive
passages: A 60–80 word answer to "{title}" that answers the precise long-tail question
Technical specifics a generalist could not produce: commands, attribute names, permission strings, MITRE technique IDs, event IDs
Edge cases and exceptions
How to detect or verify it in your own environment

formats.label: How-to Guide
passages: The whole procedure for {title} compressed to 60 words, or the step count plus the outcome
Prerequisites: permissions, tools and access level
Numbered steps in order, each with the action, why it matters and the expected result
How to verify it worked, and a symptom → cause → fix troubleshooting table

formats.label: Framework
passages: The framework in 60 words: its stable name, its stages, and what it is for
A table of stages, then one section per stage: what it is, what you do, what you produce, how you know you're done
How the framework maps to established standards (MITRE ATT&CK, CIS, NIST, ANSSI)
An adoption path: where to start

formats.label: Template
passages: What the template contains, as a list
The template rendered in full on the page as a table or structured list, not only a download
Field-by-field guidance with a worked example for each field
A filled-in example

formats.label: Checklist
passages: The item count, what the checklist covers and who it is for
The checklist grouped into 4–8 named sections; every item a yes/no imperative with one line of why
Priority tiering: critical, important, recommended
Scoring and what your result means

formats.label: Comparison (Concept)
passages: The distinction in one or two sentences, stated outright
A comparison table high on the page: 6–10 rows of real dimensions, substantive cells, never checkmarks
Where the two genuinely overlap
When to use which, and whether you need both

formats.label: Comparison (Vendor)
passages: Who each vendor is genuinely best for, with a real concession
An at-a-glance comparison table: architecture, deployment, coverage, remediation, time to value, pricing model, best fit
What the competitor does well, placed before the company's case
Choose [competitor] if… / choose the company if…

formats.label: Alternatives
passages: The shortlist named, with a one-line reason for each
A summary table: vendor, best for, deployment model, differentiator, pricing model
Why teams look for alternatives, with sourced reasons
One entry per alternative with identical sub-structure, the company in a consistent slot

formats.label: Best Practices
passages: The practices named and numbered in 60–80 words
One section per practice: the imperative, why it works, how to implement and verify it, what it costs
Priority order: which three to do first
Anti-patterns: what to stop doing

formats.label: Assessment Guide
passages: What an assessment of {subject} covers and produces, in 60 words
The assessment as numbered phases: scope, collect, analyse, score, prioritise, report
A what-to-look-for table: area, what to check, what good and bad look like
A scoring model or maturity levels with observable criteria at each level

formats.label: Buyer's Guide
passages: The evaluation criteria named, in 60–80 words
Who needs this category and who does not, placed early
One section per evaluation criterion: why it matters, how to test it, a good answer, a red flag
Questions to ask every vendor, as a numbered list copy-pasteable into an RFP

formats.label: Metrics Guide
passages: The metrics named, in 60–80 words
Why the obvious metrics mislead
One section per metric: definition, the formula, data required, interpretation, benchmark range, how it gets gamed
The 3–5 numbers an executive should see

formats.label: Stats / Data
passages: The 3–5 headline figures on {subject}, stated outright with sources named inline
Key statistics as standalone sentences, each with the number, subject, source and year
A data table: statistic, figure, source, year, sample or methodology
What the data means, and a methodology and sources section

formats.label: Original Research
passages: The headline finding with its number and sample size
Methodology, early and detailed: sample, population, period, collection method, limitations
One section per finding: the finding, the data, interpretation, why it matters
Limitations and what could not be measured

formats.label: Examples
passages: The example categories named, in 60 words
A quick-reference table: example, environment, mechanism, impact, fix
One section per example with identical sub-structure, naming specific attributes, permissions or commands
Patterns across the examples

formats.label: Thought Leadership
passages: The thesis asserted plainly in 50–60 words
Why the conventional view persists, steelmanned properly
The counter-argument taken seriously, then answered
What would change the author's mind

formats.label: Tools Listicle
passages: The tools named, with a one-line reason for each
How the tools were evaluated, stated before the list
One entry per tool with identical structure including a real limitations line, the company included
What no tool solves

formats.label: Solution Page
passages: What the solution does, for whom, with what outcome, in 50 words
3–5 capability blocks, each an outcome
Proof: named customers where permitted and quantified outcomes
Deployment and integrations

formats.label: Use Case
passages: The specific problem this segment has and the outcome, in 50–60 words
Why this segment is different: constraints that are only true for it
Relevant compliance mapping for this segment
Proof from a customer in this segment

formats.label: Integration Page
passages: What the integration does and what it requires, in 50 words
What data is collected, and the exact permission or role names required
Setup as numbered steps with the real console path
Limitations: what is not covered
